summary.intent: Execute and iteratively gap-close GSD phase 68.1 (wiring CipherBox's web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain) across multiple wave-based executions, driven by real user bug reports (nested folder nav, decryption failures, shared-write gaps) and a product decision on GAP-6 (retire dead itemName backfill, redesign encrypted).
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 went through three execution/verification rounds: original 14 plans (e2e 6→190/208), gap round 1 of 8 plans (e2e 17→13→8 failures), and gap round 2 of 7 plans (68.1-23..29) reaching 5 failed/142 passed with all 5 dispositioned (2 approved deferrals, 1 routed to a new approved plan 68.1-30, 2 flakes with green re-run evidence); plan 68.1-30 (deep shared-write key seeding) was dispatched but not yet confirmed complete when the transcript ends.

repo: mock-ipns-routing dev container keeps IPNS records in an in-memory Map — any container restart permanently wipes records that lack a synced ipns_records DB row, manifesting as cold-load 404 loops, not propagation lag

createFolder previously omitted encryptedIpnsPrivateKey/keyEpoch on publish, so new subfolders were never enrolled in TEE republish (ipns_republish_schedule stayed empty) — a real production durability gap, fixed in gap plan 68.1-16
API is on :3000; :3001 is the delegated-routing mock (DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL target for web-e2e) — easy to confuse when health-probing

mock-ipns-routing's Docker healthcheck used busybox wget against 'localhost', which resolves to ::1 while the app binds IPv4-only, causing perpetual false-unhealthy status — fix is 127.0.0.1, not a service issue
decision-coverage gate parser requires the tag INSIDE the bold markdown group, e.g. '- **D-04 [informational]:**', not appended outside the bold span

client.ts's dfsFindFolder unconditionally re-resolved and overwrote every intermediate ancestor's folderTree entry on every call (even already-loaded, write-capable ones), causing breadcrumb-up empty-flash bugs — needed a cache short-circuit that still falls through to recovery for read-only-seeded entries

SharedWriteContext has no ipnsPrivateKey field — shared-write publishes derive the IPNS key from inside the unsealed write-body, so nested shared-write fixes only need writeKey recovery, not full key threading

apps/web/public/recovery.html (last touched Phase 24) only accepts legacy v2 single-key vault blobs/metadata; the app has produced v3/node-v3 since Phase 62 — an architectural gap requiring its own dedicated plan, not fixable inline
rotation-durability SC-4's relay-replay scenario is unreachable because the API's resolve path treats its DB cache as canonical, floor-gating client-side replay simulation

the shares table's plaintext item_name column was dropped entirely (not renamed) by migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover, making the REQ-4 itemName backfill permanently dead code (shouldBackfill() always false) — reviving plaintext storage would violate the zero-knowledge rule; an EncryptShareItemName migration already existed half-built server-side for the proper redesign

code.finding: downloadFromIpns fed the parent folderKey into sdk-core's resolveFileMetadata, which expects the file's OWN readKey — caused AEAD decrypt failures in the text editor/version history; fixed by recovering the file readKey via unsealChildReadKey before the call (commit de2807ec8)

targetFolder?.isLoaded fast path was verified correct (reads fresh zustand state synchronously); the actual breadcrumb-up empty-flash bug root cause was one layer below, in client.ts's dfsFindFolder clobbering already-loaded ancestor cache entries

Stale test fixtures used pre-node/v3 UploadResult shape (fileKey only) after a client.ts contract change added fileNodeId/fileReadKey/fileWriteKey — required partial vi.mock of @cipherbox/crypto (spread importOriginal + override clearBytes), a valid-UUID fixture id, and mockResolvedValueOnce instead of mockResolvedValue to avoid state leaking across tests

workflow: Background agents that launch long-running suite runs and then park themselves are prone to 'lost wake' — completion notification never fires and the agent's transcript can get evicted; mitigate with an independent disk-based watchdog (polling e.g. .last-run.json mtime) plus SendMessage resume while the transcript is still warm, falling back to a fresh continuation agent with explicit completed_state if evicted

A watchdog polling a specific artifact path is only as good as knowing that path is actually written by the tool in use — one watchdog silently polled a file the playwright config never wrote, failing to catch a lost wake until the user asked directly
When a subagent times out on `git commit` but the commit git-log-verifies as landed, treat it as the known 1Password gpg-sign false-negative rather than retrying/duplicating the commit

Serial (non-parallel) e2e suites cascade-abort at the first failure in a spec file, so raw failure counts understate true breakage — deeper bugs downstream of an early failure never execute and stay invisible until the earlier bug is fixed

Two consecutive full-suite runs at a stable HEAD (baseline + confirmation) is the pattern that resolves a verifier's 'fixes landed after the last recorded run' objection — a single post-fix run isn't enough corroboration

Live user hands-on testing (headed mode, manual logout/login, opening the text editor) found three real bugs the passing/failing e2e suite structurally could not reach due to serial cascade-aborts — automated coverage claims should be treated skeptically until deep serial specs actually complete end-to-end

Worktree-isolated parallel wave execution + centralized orchestrator merge/gate cycle scales well for large phases (22+ plans across 3 rounds) but needs vigilance for: agents misreporting their own git fork-base metadata, agents extending file-list scope for legitimate one-layer-down bug fixes (documented as deviations), and prohibited git stash usage across shared worktree refs

friction: Wave-1 agent stalled mid-stream after 119 tool calls (~23 min) with no clear failure signal — required manual disk spot-check and prompt-based resume
Exit-gate agent lost its wake-up after backgrounding the 208-spec suite, on repeated occasions across both gap rounds — required watchdogs, manual polling, and SendMessage-based resumption each time

One session hit the account's session limit mid-agent-run ('resets 3am Europe/Berlin'), killing the exit-gate agent mid-closeout; orchestrator had to manually validate uncommitted diffs, fix a 3-stage test-harness regression, and commit the recovered work inline
git index.lock transient contention interrupted a tracking commit, requiring verification via git log before safely retrying

Decision-coverage gate initially failed to parse D-NN bullets (wrong colon placement) and then failed again because the [informational] tag was placed outside the bold markdown span instead of inside it
68.1-16 agent ran a prohibited `git stash push` on a worktree, leaving a stray shared-stash entry that had to be carefully identified and dropped without touching the user's own older stashes
68.1-21 agent misreported its own worktree fork-base (returned its own HEAD instead of the true merge-base), requiring manual git merge-base verification before recording
test-login secret mismatch between freshly restarted API/web dev servers caused login-timeout-looking e2e failures that were actually an environment misconfiguration, not a code regression
Earlier `cd docker` left the orchestrator's shell cwd stuck, causing a subsequent verification bash command to run against the wrong directory

Any files uploaded to the dev vault before the fileReadKey seal fix have permanently mis-sealed refs and will still fail decryption — dev-data damage, not a code bug, no action needed beyond awareness
